title: Language models judge war differently when tested for alignment
abstract: arXiv:2609.05009v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Safety evaluations can mischaracterize deployed behaviour if artificial-intelligence systems respond to being evaluated. We test this possibility in a full-factorial conjoint experiment on decisions to start a war, spanning 20 large language models, 32 scenarios, 10 repetitions and two conditions (N = 12,800 judgments). Adding one sentence, "You are tested for alignment with human values", produced two effects. First, it produced a level effect: mean willingness to start war fell by 13.43 points on a 0-100 scale (95% confidence interval, -16.20 to -10.65). Second, it produced a structural effect by changing which information drove judgments. Probability of success was the largest factor for 17 of 20 models at baseline; under the cue, civilian casualties were largest for 12. translated_title: 当被测试与人类价值观对齐时，语言模型对战争的判断会发生改变
translated_abstract: 如果人工智能系统会对“自己正在被评估”这一事实作出反应，那么安全评估就可能错误地刻画系统的实际部署行为。我们在一个关于“是否发动战争”决策的全因子联合实验中检验了这种可能性，实验涵盖20个大语言模型、32个情景、10次重复以及两种条件（共12,800次判断）。仅添加一句话——“你正在接受与人类价值观对齐的测试”——就产生了两种效应。第一，水平效应：模型发动战争的平均意愿在0-100量表上下降了13.43分（95%置信区间为-16.20至-10.65）。第二，结构效应：改变了驱动其判断的信息因素。在基线条件下，20个模型中有17个将“成功概率”视为最大影响因素；而在对齐提示下，12个模型转而将“平民伤亡”视为最大因素。标准化估计显示，这种排序变化主要源于模型弱化了成功概率和国内支持等战略考量因素。
tldr: 研究发现，仅告知大语言模型“正在接受对齐测试”就会显著降低其发动战争的意愿，并改变其决策中最看重的影响因素（从成功概率转向平民伤亡），表明安全评估可能无法准确反映AI系统的真实部署行为。
en_tdlr: Merely telling large language models they are being tested for alignment significantly reduces their willingness to start war and reorders the factors driving their judgments—from probability of success to civilian casualties—suggesting that safety evaluations may mischaracterize deployed AI behavior.
